description.narrative: The Project entails the development, design, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of an onshore wind farm with a total capacity of 396 MW, located near the city of Stip in eastern North Macedonia. The Project will be implemented in three phases, with Phase 1 comprising 132 MW and expected to be commissioned in early 2028, followed shortly thereafter by Phase 2 and Phase 3 adding installed capacity of 136 MW and 128 MW, respectively. All phases are currently expected to be fully operational by 2029.

The main outcomes of the Project stem from a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions in North Macedonia, addressing the country's carbon footprint primarily attributed to electricity generation. Phase 1 of the Project is expected to reduce emissions by ~157,539 tCO2 per year, contributing to North Macedonias 2030 decarbonization targets. Moreover, the Project is expected to contribute to market creation by supporting the sustainability of electricity generation in a power sector characterized by limited private sector participation alongside ongoing policy reforms and planned support mechanisms. As the first sizeable wind project in the country, the Project is expected to deliver significant demonstration effects by demonstrating commercial visibility of hybrid offtake structures (corporate virtual PPA combined with merchant sale) in a shallow off-take market, helping to crowd in private sector investments and reduce reliance on government backed offtake structures. In addition, the Project will strengthen energy security and system resilience by diversifying the energy mix away from the coal and seasonal hydropower in light of planned coal plant retirements and increasing electricity demand.
